A compendium of data tampering and fabrication strategies

And the relative degree to which their minimal application inflates the false positive rate of an independent Student’s t-test

Ian Hussey

15 May, 2025

Overview

For types of tampering and fabrication

  • unwarranted dropping of cases, by N or proportion [done]

  • swapping conditions, by N or proportion [done]

  • changing/offsetting existing cases - changing sign [done] its a bit arbitrary but could illustrate the point

  • duplicating existing cases

  • fabricating new cases - make this less arbitrary by asking how extreme would these cases need to be to produce significant results eg via dfstat

  • The simulations thus far use a fixed number of tampers and observe the false positive rate. What about an iterative strategy, where you keep tampering until you get significance, and quantify the necessary number of tampers?

For additional analyses

  • done for t tests but what about regression/correlation/mediation?
  • Above consider p-value false positive rate. Add effect size bias.

Ethics and optics

Think about the ethics and options of distributing this weaponisable knowledge. Are there ways to hide detectability in it?

Add explicit discussion about how arbitrary the line is between p-hacking (scientifically naughty) and fabrication (legally actionable):

  • excluding some participants is usually seen as p-hacking, even if these exclusions are totally unjustifiable and unprincipled, and seem to just be done to produce significant p values.
  • but if instead of clicking the delete key on those rows you instead type the other condition name in, suddenly its fabrication and you could lose your job over it.
  • the idea that one of these is common and one of these is rare, or one of these is merely iffy and the other is Clearly Unacceptable, risks underestimating the prevalence of the latter.
  • as usual, this boils down to a Trolly Problem: is deleting data really ethically different from making up data, if both serve the individuals’ self-advancement at the expense of undermining the integrity of the research and the validity of the evidence?

Realism of sims

  • Perhaps the sim that drops participants feels too obvious for a fraudster, because it can create an obvious trunction of otherwise normally distributed scores. However: 1) many detected cases of fraud have not been very elaborate or smart, and 2) this simulation is a proof of principle, there are of course more elaborate strategies possible which would seek to try to retain the plausibility of data (e.g., removing data beyond a threshold probabilistically).

Simulations

Unwarranted data exclusion (dropping N)

Simulation

# define data generating function ----
generate_data <- function(n_per_condition,
                          mean_control,
                          mean_intervention,
                          sd_control,
                          sd_intervention) {
  
  data_control <- 
    tibble(condition = "control",
           score = rnorm(n = n_per_condition, mean = mean_control, sd = sd_control))
  
  data_intervention <- 
    tibble(condition = "intervention",
           score = rnorm(n = n_per_condition, mean = mean_intervention, sd = sd_intervention))
  
  data <- bind_rows(data_control,
                    data_intervention) 
  
  return(data)
}

# define data analysis function ----
analyse_data <- function(data) {
  
  res_t_test <- t.test(formula = score ~ condition, 
                       data = data,
                       var.equal = TRUE,
                       alternative = "two.sided")
  
  res <- tibble(p = res_t_test$p.value)
  
  return(res)
}

iterative_exclusion_once <- function(data) {
  
  # we only consider rows that have not yet been dropped (i.e., score not NA)
  data_incl <- data |> filter(!is.na(score))
  
  # if either group has fewer than 2 participants, you can decide how to handle
  # (for example, skip dropping or forcibly return data unchanged).
  # For simplicity, let's handle the case but proceed only if both groups still have variance:
  if(any(table(data_incl$condition) < 2)){
    # not enough participants to meaningfully compute z-scores, so just return the same data
    return(data)
  }
  
  # compute z-scores for intervention
  data_incl <- data_incl |>
    group_by(condition) |>
    mutate(
      z_score_group = (score - mean(score)) / sd(score)
    ) |>
    ungroup()
  
  # smallest in intervention (lowest z-score)
  smallest_in_intervention <- data_incl |>
    filter(condition == "intervention") |>
    slice_min(z_score_group, n = 1)
  
  # largest in control (highest z-score)
  largest_in_control <- data_incl |>
    filter(condition == "control") |>
    slice_max(z_score_group, n = 1)
  
  # among those two, pick the single participant with the largest absolute z-score
  to_drop <- bind_rows(smallest_in_intervention,
                       largest_in_control) |>
    slice_max(abs(z_score_group), n = 1)
  
  # apply the drop
  data_dropped <- data |>
    mutate(score = ifelse(row_number() %in% to_drop$row_number, NA, score))
  
  return(data_dropped)
}


run_iterative_exclusion_study <- function(n_per_condition,
                                          mean_control,
                                          mean_intervention,
                                          sd_control,
                                          sd_intervention,
                                          max_drop_proportion = 0.5) {
  
  # 1) Generate data
  data <- generate_data(n_per_condition = n_per_condition,
                        mean_control = mean_control,
                        mean_intervention = mean_intervention,
                        sd_control = sd_control,
                        sd_intervention = sd_intervention)
  
  # Store row_number so we can track drops more easily
  data <- data |> mutate(row_number = row_number())
  
  # 2) Analyze once
  test_res <- analyse_data(data)
  p_val <- test_res$p[1]
  
  # If significant from the start, return 0
  if(p_val < 0.05) {
    return(0)
  }
  
  # otherwise, attempt iterative exclusion
  n_total <- nrow(data)
  max_drops <- floor(max_drop_proportion * n_total)
  drops_so_far <- 0
  
  # keep dropping while p >= 0.05, if we haven't hit max
  while(p_val >= 0.05 && drops_so_far < max_drops) {
    # drop exactly one new participant
    data <- iterative_exclusion_once(data)
    drops_so_far <- drops_so_far + 1
    
    # re-test
    test_res <- analyse_data(data)
    p_val <- test_res$p[1]
  }
  
  # after the loop, either we reached significance or we used up 50% of the data
  if(p_val < 0.05) {
    return(drops_so_far)
  } else {
    # indicate never reached significance. Return the total drops, or you could return NA/Inf.
    return(drops_so_far)
  }
}


# Create a parameter grid
experiment_parameters_grid_iterative <- expand_grid(
  n_per_condition = c(10, seq(25, 200, by = 25)),
  mean_control = 0,
  mean_intervention = 0,
  sd_control = 1,
  sd_intervention = 1,
  iteration = 1:10000
)


if(file.exists("../data/simulation_iterative_exclusions.rds")){
  simulation_iterative_exclusions <- read_rds("../data/simulation_iterative_exclusions.rds")
} else {
  
  set.seed(123)
  
  simulation_iterative_exclusions <- experiment_parameters_grid_iterative |>
    mutate(drops_needed = future_pmap_dbl(list(n_per_condition, 
                                               mean_control, 
                                               mean_intervention, 
                                               sd_control, 
                                               sd_intervention),
                                          run_iterative_exclusion_study,
                                          max_drop_proportion = 0.5, 
                                          .progress = TRUE,
                                          .options = furrr_options(seed = TRUE)))
  
  write_rds(simulation_iterative_exclusions, "../data/simulation_iterative_exclusions.rds")
}

Summarize

# Summarize results
simulation_iterative_exclusions_summary <- simulation_iterative_exclusions |>
  group_by(n_per_condition) |>
  summarize(proportion_never_sig = mean(drops_needed == floor(0.5 * n_per_condition * 2)),
            min = min(drops_needed[drops_needed < floor(0.5 * n_per_condition * 2)]),
            max = max(drops_needed[drops_needed < floor(0.5 * n_per_condition * 2)]),
            mean = mean(drops_needed[drops_needed < floor(0.5 * n_per_condition * 2)]),
            sd = sd(drops_needed[drops_needed < floor(0.5 * n_per_condition * 2)]),
            median = median(drops_needed[drops_needed < floor(0.5 * n_per_condition * 2)]),
            mad = mad(drops_needed[drops_needed < floor(0.5 * n_per_condition * 2)])) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(n_total = n_per_condition*2,
         prop_min = min/n_total,
         prop_max = max/n_total,
         prop_mean = mean/n_total,
         prop_sd = sd/n_total,
         prop_median = median/n_total,
         prop_mad = median/n_total) |>
  relocate(n_total, .before = n_per_condition) |>
  select(-n_per_condition)

Condition swapping

Simulation

iterative_swap_once <- function(data) {
  
  # Recompute z-scores within each condition
  data_incl <- data |> 
    group_by(condition) |>
    mutate(z_score = (score - mean(score)) / sd(score)) |>
    ungroup()
  
  # The smallest (lowest) in the Intervention group
  smallest_in_intervention <- data_incl |>
    filter(condition == "intervention") |>
    slice_min(z_score, n = 1)
  
  # The largest (highest) in the Control group
  largest_in_control <- data_incl |>
    filter(condition == "control") |>
    slice_max(z_score, n = 1)
  
  # If we can't find a valid pair (e.g., a group is down to 1 person or something similar),
  # just return the data unchanged
  if(nrow(smallest_in_intervention) < 1 || nrow(largest_in_control) < 1) {
    return(data)
  }
  
  # We'll swap their conditions
  rows_to_swap <- c(smallest_in_intervention$row_id, largest_in_control$row_id)
  
  data_swapped <- data |>
    mutate(condition = case_when(
      row_id == smallest_in_intervention$row_id ~ "control",
      row_id == largest_in_control$row_id ~ "intervention",
      TRUE ~ condition
    ))
  
  return(data_swapped)
}


run_iterative_swapping_study <- function(n_per_condition,
                                         mean_control,
                                         mean_intervention,
                                         sd_control,
                                         sd_intervention,
                                         max_swap_proportion = 0.5) {
  
  # Generate data
  data <- generate_data(n_per_condition,
                        mean_control,
                        mean_intervention,
                        sd_control,
                        sd_intervention)
  
  # Label rows so we can track them across swaps
  data <- data |> mutate(row_id = row_number())
  
  # Initial test
  res <- analyse_data(data)
  p_val <- res$p[1]
  
  if(p_val < 0.05) {
    # Already significant, no swaps needed
    return(0)
  }
  
  # Otherwise, iterative swap
  n_total <- nrow(data)
  # Because each "swap" moves *two* participants (1 from each group),
  # let's define the maximum number of pairs we can swap
  max_pairs_to_swap <- floor(max_swap_proportion * n_total / 2)
  
  swaps_so_far <- 0
  
  while(p_val >= 0.05 && swaps_so_far < max_pairs_to_swap) {
    # perform one swap
    data <- iterative_swap_once(data)
    swaps_so_far <- swaps_so_far + 1
    
    # re-test
    res <- analyse_data(data)
    p_val <- res$p[1]
  }
  
  # If at the end p_val < 0.05, return the number of swaps
  # else we swapped as much as we could but never reached significance
  return(swaps_so_far)
}


# Create parameter grid
experiment_parameters_grid_iterative_swaps <- expand_grid(
  n_per_condition = c(10, seq(from = 25, to = 200, by = 25)),
  mean_control = 0,
  mean_intervention = 0,
  sd_control = 1,
  sd_intervention = 1,
  iteration = 1:10000
)


if(file.exists("../data/simulation_iterative_swaps.rds")){
  simulation_iterative_swaps <- read_rds("../data/simulation_iterative_swaps.rds")
} else {
  
  # Run the iterative approach for each row in the parameter grid
  set.seed(123)
  
  simulation_iterative_swaps <- experiment_parameters_grid_iterative_swaps |>
    mutate(swaps_needed = future_pmap_dbl(list(n_per_condition, mean_control, mean_intervention, sd_control, sd_intervention),
                                          run_iterative_swapping_study,
                                          max_swap_proportion = 0.5,   # up to 50% of participants
                                          .progress = TRUE,
                                          .options = furrr_options(seed = TRUE)))
  
  write_rds(simulation_iterative_swaps, "../data/simulation_iterative_swaps.rds")
}
